## Completion evidence

**Deliverable:** `docs/adr/0107-reconciler-typed-mutation-payload-contract.md` (renumbered
from 0106 mid-flight — a concurrent, unrelated ADR 0106 "remote-anchored history
reclamation" landed on `origin/main` while this ticket's plan review/claim/drafting was in
progress; rebased and renumbered to 0107 before push, no content changes needed beyond the
number and title).

**Census (Serena + grep, reconciled):** Walked every producer/consumer of `Mutation.payload`
across `mutation.py`, `outbound_mutation_builders.py`, `outbound_differ.py`,
`batch_dispatch.py`, `applier.py`/`apply_base.py`, `typed_dispatch.py`, `apply_inbound.py`,
`apply_outbound.py`, `differ.py`, `observation.py`, `ticket_plan.py`, and
`outbound_field_diff.py` using Serena `find_referencing_symbols`/`find_symbol` for call-graph
edges, and `grep` for string-literal/dynamic-load/monkeypatch sites (per this repo's own
documented Serena/grep asymmetry). Key finding: `_VALID_COMBINATIONS` enumerates 12
`(direction, action)` pairs but only 10 are wired in `typed_dispatch._LEAVES`;
`(inbound, delete)` and `(inbound, probe)` are dead-by-design (removed by bug 3b5f, per
`apply_inbound.py`'s own module docstring, referencing ADR 0028) — flagged as a deletion
target, not something to type.

**Design:** A discriminated payload union keyed by `(direction, action)`, one named contract
per each of the 10 live combinations (required/optional fields + validation ownership), with
canonical-bytes-vs-comparison-only representations distinguished explicitly. Ownership of
validation, canonical serialization, adapter projection, follow-ons, binding identity, and
provider-neutral outcomes assigned to existing owners; ADR 0103 reaffirmed as sole
retry/idempotency/fuse owner.

**Producer-seam disposition:** The `_compute_outbound_update_mutation` 23-parameter seam
(17 positional + 6 kwonly) and its `compute_update_fields` (14-value) /
`diff_canonical_fields` (11-value) collaborators are dispositioned into four *existing*
cohesive owners — `OutboundDiffConfig`, `Observation`/`TicketPlan`, the Backend-port
collaborators, and the observability sinks — explicitly rejecting a new generic
context/wrapper object per the ticket's own trap warning.

**Migration sequencing:** expand -> compare (shadow, side-effect-free) -> cut (live, isolated
Jira targets, no production dual-send) -> delete, with `_mutation_to_batch_dict`, the legacy
batch-dict dispatch path, the two coexisting CREATE payload shapes in `batch_dispatch.py`, and
obsolete compatibility re-exports/tests named as explicit deletion targets. Anchored to this
repo's own documented expand/contract practice (`docs/migrations.md`; ADR 0060/0098/0100
precedent) rather than inventing new terminology.

**ADR reconciliation:** Checked against ADRs 0004, 0026-0029, 0083, 0092, 0098, 0103 — none
decide the `Mutation.payload` representation boundary, confirming a new ADR was warranted per
the story's own Scope note. Three existing in-repo discriminated-union precedents were found
and cited as the pattern this design follows (not inventing a new abstraction):
`mutation.py`'s own `MutationDirection`/`MutationAction` allowlist, `common.schema.json`'s
`"kind"` discriminator, `llm/usage_log.py`'s explicit outcome discriminator.

**Governance disposition (important, explicit judgment call):** ADR 0107 is recorded as
**Proposed (DRAFT)**, not Accepted. This autonomous agent session has no human reviewer
present and per the architecture-decisions skill/lifecycle (RESEARCH -> DRAFT -> HOLD ->
MERGE) cannot self-certify a MERGE. The ADR text and this comment both state explicitly:
**the dependent implementation story (`earthborn-statuelike-boutu`) must not begin until a
human operator reviews ADR 0107 and moves it to Accepted.** This is treated as satisfying
AC8's "otherwise" branch (recording *why* the gate is open) rather than fabricating approval.

**No implementation/code changes made** — this is a research/design-record deliverable per
the ticket's own Testing section ("This story produces architecture evidence rather than
production behavior"); no `src/`/`tests/` files were touched, consistent with the sibling
research ticket `c465`'s precedent in this epic.

**Validation run (all green):**
- `scripts/check_adr_numbers.py` — clean (bijection holds, incl. after 0106->0107 rename).
- `scripts/gen_adr_index.py --check` — clean.
- `make lint` — fully passed (ruff check/format, complexity baseline, config-ownership/reads,
  comment hygiene, shellcheck, zizmor security scan, DCO identity, etc.).
- Targeted tests `tests/scripts/test_check_adr_numbers.py`,
  `tests/scripts/test_check_adr_numbers_heldout.py`, `tests/unit/test_gerrit_docs_only.py` —
  27/27 passed.
- `rebar-get_verify_commands` — empty (no ticket-level custom verify commands); CI's
  `documentation gates (docs-only route)` job independently re-ran and passed the same
  ADR-number/index checks.

**Gerrit change:** https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2405 — **MERGED**.
Patch set 1 (as ADR 0106) got `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`; a Gerrit-side conflict
(add/add on `docs/adr/.numbers/0106`) was discovered before submit because a different ADR
0106 had landed concurrently on `origin/main` — resolved by rebasing onto `origin/main` and
renumbering to ADR 0107 (file rename, in-file title update, `.numbers/0107` marker, regenerated
`docs/adr/README.md`), re-validated (`make lint` + targeted tests green again), and re-pushed
as patch set 2 (same Change-Id). Patch set 2 independently earned fresh `LLM-Review +1` (1
non-blocking advisory: a phrasing nit about the combination-count arithmetic, not a
correctness issue) and `Verified +1`, then was Submitted and merged to Gerrit's `main`
(commit `185458ae5c7d`).

**AC-by-AC:** all 8 Acceptance Criteria checked off in the ticket description with inline
justification pointing to the relevant ADR 0107 section (see description diff).
